notes: §2002:15.75.2 AR1 admits an alphanumeric literal (LIT), a national literal (NATLIT), and data items of class alphanumeric (ITEM PIC X; EDIT numeric-edited, class alphanumeric by §2002:8.5.2 Table 3) or national (NAT PIC N). Each is accepted; by §2002:15.75.3 RV1 the conforming contents (per the NUMVAL argument format) return 0 and the BAD content returns the position of the first character in error: LIT=000 NATLIT=000 ITEM=000 EDIT=000 NAT=000 BAD=002. Refused: PIC 9(3) (class numeric), PIC S9(3) USAGE NATIONAL (class numeric at 2002 by kb/Work PB5625 reading B). Run at --std 2002 with the pinned build of dc1f2dcce8: output equals the derived golden. A PIC A argument (class alphabetic) is ADMITTED at 2002: "An alphabetic data item may be specified wherever an elementary alphanumeric data item is permitted as an operand" (§2002:8.5.2.1; kb/Work PB5615, through EditionInfo.AlphabeticIsAlphanumeric in IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation); the 2002 refusal of it written by the golden-2002-9 integrator was withdrawn when PB5615 merged main, and the refusal from 2014 is pb5615-alphabetic-operands-refused.
